title: Each download of a raw dataset writes its own temporary file
request: Found while checking the quick gate of 28.8: a test file failed in a fresh worktree although it passed alone.
spec: dclab_rnd/expansion/datasets.py (the pinned raw files of the public datasets, downloaded once and checked by hash)
plan: Reproduce the failure with two downloads of one file at once.
Give every writer its own temporary name, and leave no temporary file behind.

decisions.decision: The temporary name carries the process and the thread, and the last whole copy replaces the file.
decisions.why: A lock across processes would need a lock file of its own; two whole copies of a pinned file are identical, and the hash is checked after the download.

findings.defect: Two test files that read one public dataset at once in a fresh checkout failed one of them.
findings.scenario: In a new worktree with no cached downloads, two test processes fetched the same raw file together; the first renamed the shared temporary file and the second found it gone.
findings.cause: Every writer used the same temporary name beside the file.
findings.fix: Each writer writes its own temporary file and removes it whatever happens; the rename is atomic, so either whole copy is the file.

outcome: Concurrent downloads of one pinned file both succeed and leave only the file.
lessons: A temporary file beside its target needs a name of its own per writer when tests run in parallel.
risks: Two processes that start together still both download the file: the time is spent twice, not the result.
